meta.note: Good practices were found by web search in October 2026. One-line takeaways are in our own words and based on the page that was read. Items marked as not read were listed from titles only. Ten sources were added on 2026-11-08 (six peer-reviewed), each read on its page, abstract or report.

sources.title: WOAH Observatory annual report 2022, key findings: PVS Pathway
sources.takeaway: 448 PVS activities in 2006 to 2021 (Africa 208), an analysis of levels of advancement for 43 Members (2016-2021) and signs of decreasing interest in PVS Follow-up and Gap Analysis missions.

sources.title: Overview of the PVS Pathway
sources.takeaway: Four steps (orientation, PVS Evaluation, planning, targeted support) and the tools for each, including PVS Gap Analysis 2.0 and the strategic planning template.

sources.title: The OIE PVS Tool: quick overview of the 45 critical competencies
sources.takeaway: Lists all competencies under the four fundamental components.

sources.title: One Health capacity building (PVS Pathway)
sources.takeaway: Explains IHR-PVS National Bridging Workshops run with FAO and WHO, the four steps, and that PVS experts join JEE missions where PVS missions have taken place.

sources.title: IHR-PVS National Bridging Workshop fact sheet
sources.takeaway: Three-day workshop; 16 joint technical areas; works best after a JEE and before a national action plan; ends in a joint roadmap.

sources.title: Participant handbook, National Bridging Workshop: capitalizing on IHR and PVS (version 7.0)
sources.takeaway: Participant guide for the three-day workshop: seven sessions taking human, animal and environmental health from One Health concepts and a gap review across 16 technical areas to a joint operational roadmap.

sources.title: National Bridging Workshop on the IHR and the OIE PVS Pathway: Kyrgyzstan (Bishkek, 2-4 October 2018)
sources.takeaway: Health and veterinary services agreed a joint roadmap: an intersectoral committee on zoonoses with focal points at oblast and rayon level, a joint surveillance strategy and shared database, harmonised laboratory methods, and joint outbreak response and risk communication.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the report's roadmap section.

sources.title: Report of the National Bridging Workshop on the IHR and the OIE PVS Pathway, Pakistan (Islamabad, 9-11 May 2017)
sources.takeaway: Top priority was a formal One Health coordination mechanism, with One Health hubs at federal, provincial and district level, a harmonised laboratory information system and joint surveillance piloted at district level.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the report's summary.

sources.title: Integrating wildlife health through IHR-PVS National Bridging Workshops
sources.takeaway: Slides showing how a wildlife health session is built into the bridging workshops (more than 60 held so far, each ending in a joint roadmap), using an avian influenza scenario with wild bird die-offs.

sources.title: Independent review of PVS Pathway reports from African Member Countries: final report
sources.authors: Weaver Consulting International, Intiga Consulting, Colibri Consulting (for OIE)
sources.takeaway: Desk review of PVS Evaluation and Follow-up reports: little overall change in levels of advancement across Africa, with persistent gaps in veterinary staffing, laboratory quality assurance, risk analysis, food safety, traceability, veterinary medicines and funding; confidentiality of reports limits their use.

sources.title: Evaluation of the PVS Pathway programme: final report
sources.takeaway: The PVS Pathway is valued but often under-used because reports are not acted on or shared; publishing reports, digitising data and more frequent follow-ups would raise its impact.

sources.title: The Observatory's monitoring: towards better emergency preparedness
sources.takeaway: Global data on contingency plans (73% for avian influenza, 24% for ASF), 466 reported simulation exercises and PVS scores on emergency funding and response; recommends regular, reported exercises.

sources.title: Implementation of WOAH Standards: the Second Observatory Monitoring Report
sources.takeaway: Five-yearly review of how Members apply WOAH standards on trade and sanitary measures, self-declaration, movement control and zoning, with the gaps that hold back safe trade.

sources.title: Use, challenges and impact of zoning and compartmentalisation. Part 1: zones for avian influenza, African swine fever and foot and mouth disease, 2018–2022
sources.takeaway: Member survey: zoning mainly used for outbreak response and trade, held back by staffing, biosecurity enforcement and labs; trading partners' acceptance can take over two years and rests on trust in certification.

sources.title: Evaluation of the collaborative process of public-private partnerships in the veterinary domain: the case of the Sanitary Mandate in Tunisia
sources.authors: Dhaoui A, Poupaud M, Zargouni S, Dieuzy-Labaye I, Ferchiou A, Peyre M
sources.takeaway: Participatory evaluation of Tunisia's delegation of vaccination campaigns to private vets: good coverage gains, but private vets felt left out of decisions and communication, and there were no performance indicators.

sources.title: Veterinary Council twinning between South Africa and Tanzania concluded
sources.takeaway: An 18-month twinning with the South African council helped Tanzania's veterinary statutory body adopt Day One competencies, mandatory CPD, practice registration, a registrant database and a strategic plan.

sources.title: Methodologies to assess community-based animal health workers curricula and training programs: a mini review
sources.authors: Matos A, Hoet AE, Bessler AL, et al.
sources.takeaway: Only 7 of 203 publications assessed CAHW training in a structured way; the authors map them to the Kirkpatrick model to guide a tool for checking programmes against WOAH's CAHW competency guidelines.

sources.title: Report of the pre-workshop veterinary workforce survey, Southern Africa
sources.authors: Oosthuizen J, Muleke C, Ameda B (WOAH)
sources.takeaway: Survey of veterinary services in the region on the mix of veterinarians, veterinary paraprofessionals and community animal health workers, as input to WOAH's Veterinary Workforce Development programme.

sources.title: Public-private partnerships in the veterinary domain (PVS Pathway targeted support)
sources.takeaway: WOAH's support option for building partnerships between veterinary services and private actors, for example to deliver vaccination campaigns.

sources.title: Piloting a livestock identification and traceability system in the northern Tanzania–Narok–Nairobi trade route
sources.authors: Mutua F, Kihara A, Rogena J, et al.
sources.takeaway: Ear-tagged 741 cattle from primary markets to slaughterhouses with an online database (4,260 records) and tested meat for drug residues, showing that cross-border traceability is feasible along an informal beef chain.

sources.title: Surveillance and control of African swine fever in the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, March–May 2020: a multi-country e-survey
sources.takeaway: Respondents from 24 countries kept essential ASF surveillance and control going during COVID-19 restrictions by adapting it; communication was named as the first thing to improve for future crises.

sources.title: African swine fever outbreak exercise (Exercise Ivy): evaluation
sources.takeaway: Evaluation of an exercise that tested Scotland's plans for an ASF outbreak, with a summary of the lessons identified for contingency planning.

sources.title: Evaluations of the Disease Surveillance Centre network in Scotland: what parts has it reached?
sources.authors: Duncan AJ, Eze JI, Brülisauer F, et al.
sources.takeaway: Re-evaluated diagnostic submissions to the livestock surveillance network (2013–2018) with a better denominator from census and movement data, showing how reach varies with distance to a centre.

sources.title: Assessment of the biorisk status of veterinary laboratories in Southwest Nigeria: application of the FAO Laboratory Mapping Tool–Safety module
sources.authors: Adebowale O, Oduguwa A, Dipeolu S, et al.
sources.takeaway: Applied the FAO Laboratory Mapping Tool–Safety module (98 subcategories) and found biosafety and biosecurity weak across administrative, operational, engineering and PPE areas: a template for a laboratory baseline.

sources.title: A scoping review of zoonotic parasites and pathogens associated with abattoirs in Eastern Africa and recommendations for abattoirs as disease surveillance sites
sources.authors: Rodarte KA, Fair JM, Bett BK, et al.
sources.takeaway: Reviewed 104 studies across 13 countries: backyard abattoirs and slaughter slabs carry the highest zoonotic risk, and abattoirs are proposed as sentinel sites for surveillance.

sources.title: Veterinary legislation identification mission report: Mozambique
sources.takeaway: Legislation review under WOAH's Veterinary Legislation Support Programme: strong import/export and disease-control rules, but no law on laboratories, welfare or veterinary medicines and weak mandates for the competent authority.
